vibe.rationale: Vibe 4 — holding from July 16 evening's Vibe 4, stepping back up from July 16 morning's Vibe 3. The overnight July 16-17 period produces one significant new escalation category and one significant de-escalation signal that together sustain rather than shift the Vibe-4 posture. The escalation: CENTCOM struck bridges in Iran overnight, confirmed by NPR ('U.S. strikes bridges in Iran, Tehran targets U.S. bases in the Gulf' — the sixth consecutive night of strikes). Bridge targeting is a new category distinct from the coastal military corridor strikes of July 7-15 and the Tehran-periphery command-infrastructure strikes of July 15-16. Bridge and logistics interdiction signals CENTCOM is widening the target set to degrade Iran's national supply-chain architecture — potentially including Iran-Iraq border crossings — rather than merely its maritime-denial capability. This is a strategic escalation in target-set scope even if it is not a geographic escalation in the way the Tehran-periphery strikes were. However, the bridge strikes do not close the Strait, do not trigger an Iranian Hormuz closure declaration, and do not constitute a direct US-Iran surface engagement in the waterway — meaning the July 16 morning brief's explicit Vibe-3 drop criteria remain technically unmet. The de-escalation: Iranian state media circulated night-vision footage overnight claiming US Marines were captured during a failed Kharg Island landing. Multiple fact-checking organizations (IranWar.info and MEAWW) assessed the footage as having 'a very big evidence problem' with no US confirmation, no CENTCOM casualties report, and a Pentagon that declined all comment. The analyst assessment: this is Iranian psychological warfare designed to deter the Kharg Island Marine operation by creating the impression that a landing attempt already failed. The inverse signal is more analytically significant — if Iran is fabricating a failed landing, the actual operation has NOT yet occurred and Iran is working to deter it rather than respond to it. The Kharg Island Marine landing window ('within the week' per National Security Journal Pentagon sources on July 16) is now Day 2 (July 16-22), with Marine contingents not expected in theater until approximately end of July per the latest deployment reporting. This is a partial de-escalation in the immediate term: the most consequential pending ground action of the arc is not imminent today. Lebanon Pilot Zones Agreement (Rome Talks, July 16) enters Day 2 without IDF movement on Day 1 — a minor stabilizing signal in the Israel-Lebanon thread. The B and O Fire's advance to 95%+ containment (July 16 evening ICS-209) is the session's primary domestic positive — the July 17 morning ICS-209 is expected to confirm continued improvement or full containment on Day 8. WA DNR's Eastern Washington Burn Ban activates today, the most significant statewide fire management action of the east Cascades onset period. FERC AI nominal deadline is tomorrow (T-1), and the Longview CSB elevated risk window also closes tomorrow — a potential concurrent double-thread clean resolution. The September FOMC rate hike probability sits at 68.8% (CME FedWatch, July 16 evening), reflecting the Warsh three-condition adverse framework holding. Upgrade to Vibe 5 requires: Lebanon Pilot Zones confirms full south Lebanon buffer zone agreement; any credible diplomatic channel reopens (Qatar, Pakistan, EU); Kharg Island Marine landing formally delayed past July 22 window; B and O Fire 100% contained; WTI declining below $76. Maintain Vibe 4 requires: bridge targeting continues without Strait-closing or Kharg oil infrastructure escalation; Pilot Zones Day 2 clean; CISA streak holds; B and O Fire does not regress. Drop to Vibe 3 requires: bridge strikes confirmed to include oil infrastructure; IRGC 'oil for all or none' threat executed (Houthi Bab el-Mandeb activation or Gulf Arab state oil terminal attack); WTI above $87; Hezbollah mobilization confirmed. Drop to Vibe 2 requires: Kharg Island Marine landing confirmed executed and direct US-Iran ground combat confirmed; Kharg oil infrastructure struck; Iranian SNSC formal void declaration; nuclear signaling from Khamenei; WTI sustained above $92.

items.summary: The July 17 morning brief opens on the sixth consecutive night of US-Iran exchanges and a significant Iranian information operation. Three primary threads define the overnight July 16-17 period. First: the target-set escalation. CENTCOM struck bridges in Iran overnight (NPR confirmed: 'U.S. strikes bridges in Iran, Tehran targets U.S. bases in the Gulf'). CBS News confirmed this represents the sixth consecutive night of US strikes as 'battle continues over Strait of Hormuz.' Bridge targeting is analytically distinct from the prior target architecture in two ways. The July 7-15 arc targeted Iran's southern and coastal military corridor — Bandar Abbas, Jask, Chah Bahar, Bushehr, Konarak, Abu Musa — assets directly tied to maritime access and IRGC naval operations. The overnight July 15-16 Tehran-periphery strikes targeted command and political infrastructure. Bridge strikes represent a third category: logistics and supply-chain interdiction. Bridges in the Iranian context likely include Iran-Iraq border crossings (through which IRGC supplies Shia proxy networks and receives Chinese/Russian goods under sanctions circumvention), internal supply routes, and potentially infrastructure serving the Kharg Island oil export complex. This is a signal that CENTCOM is now degrading Iran's ability to sustain national ground operations and supply chains, not merely its maritime-denial or command-communication capabilities. Each successive night's target category has widened the conflict's operational scope. Second: the Iranian captured-Marines disinformation operation. Iranian state media aired night-vision footage overnight claiming US Marines were captured during a failed landing on Kharg Island. The footage reportedly showed armed personnel, flares, and a detained individual presented as an American Marine. Two fact-checking organizations analyzed the footage: IranWar.info titled its report 'The Viral Hostage Story Has a Very Big Evidence Problem,' concluding no US military operation involving a failed landing attempt by Marines has occurred. MEAWW's fact-check similarly found no evidence of the claimed event. CENTCOM has not reported any personnel losses on Kharg Island or anywhere in the Persian Gulf. The Pentagon declined all comment, which is consistent with a policy of not confirming or denying unconfirmed Iranian claims — but also consistent with having no confirmed incident to report. The analyst assessment: Iran is conducting a psychological warfare operation designed to (a) deter the Kharg Island Marine landing by making it appear already attempted and failed, (b) demonstrate to domestic audiences that Iran repelled a US assault, and (c) create uncertainty in the US decision space about whether a landing operation is still viable given alleged defenses. The inverse of this signal is the brief's primary analytical takeaway: if Iran is fabricating a failed Kharg Island landing, the actual operation has NOT yet occurred. Iran is working to deter the operation rather than respond to its execution. This is a partial de-escalation signal — the most consequential pending ground action of the arc is not in the immediate past. Third: the Kharg Island Marine landing window remains active — Day 2 of the July 16-22 'within the week' window (National Security Journal, Pentagon sources, July 16). CNN reporting indicates Iran has moved additional MANPADs and layered air defenses to Kharg Island in anticipation of a US operation. US military has deployed thousands of Marines and Navy personnel to the Middle East. The current Marine contingent arrival timeline is approximately end of July per deployment reporting, which suggests the 'within the week' window from July 16 may compress to the July 20-22 end of the stated window rather than the July 16-17 opening. The IRGC retaliation pattern on the sixth consecutive night: Tehran targeted US bases in the Gulf (per NPR). The specific targets were not confirmed in early morning reporting, but the IRGC retaliation architecture established in the July 16 brief — Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan, Oman base infrastructure — remains the operating pattern. The IRGC's 'oil for everyone or no one' ultimatum (raised July 15) remains active. The threat encompasses activation of Houthi forces to close the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which would simultaneously shut the Red Sea and Persian Gulf routes for Gulf Arab state energy exports — a threat that no IRGC action has yet executed. Its continued non-execution while six consecutive exchange nights occur suggests Iran is holding this as a maximum-leverage deterrent. The three MOU termination instruments: CENTCOM blockade (ACTIVE — Day 3); SNSC formal void declaration (STILL ABSENT); Kharg Island oil infrastructure strike (STILL ABSENT — 'decency' protection per July 13 Trump framing; Marine seizure operation as alternative now the primary pathway). Iran's strategic posture on July 17 morning: execute information warfare on Kharg, widen IRGC retaliation arc horizontally, hold the Bab el-Mandeb activation as reserve, decline negotiations ('no plans for negotiations' per FM Baghaei July 16), and await the Kharg Island decision outcome.

items.summary: Six secondary geopolitical threads on July 17 morning. First: Lebanon Pilot Zones Agreement Day 2. The July 16 Rome Talks produced a pilot zones agreement between Israel and Lebanon — a framework establishing a south Lebanon buffer zone administration mechanism. Day 1 (July 16 evening) concluded without IDF movement, suggesting the agreement is holding its opening window. The Rome Talks pilot zones framework is the most significant diplomatic development in the Israel-Lebanon thread since the Lebanon ceasefire extension on May 16. The July 17 primary monitoring question: does the IDF maintain the Day 2 posture without strike activity in the designated pilot zones? The Oman channel's destruction (July 16, IRGC radar strike) removes the back-channel that could facilitate Iran-Hezbollah sanctioning communication, creating sustained ambiguity about whether Hezbollah's posture responds to the pilot zones agreement or to Tehran's direction. Lebanon fragile hold enters Day 32. Second: World Cup Final T-2. Spain vs Argentina plays July 19 at 3 PM ET at MetLife Stadium, East Rutherford NJ. The final is the highest-attendance event of the 2026 arc at approximately 82,500 capacity plus multi-million broadcast audience. CENTCOM's FIFA-NIFC co-response posture (Day 21 active) remains at maximum alertness through the final. The brief's FIFA-specific security monitoring threads: the Seattle stadium CCTV activation ('credible threats' per July 9 brief) and the broader FIFA security architecture that has been active since the June 11 global opening remain operative through the final. Third: Russia Omsk fuel crisis Day 17. The refinery remains 75% offline; CDU-10 destroyed, CDU-11 offline. Putin's mini-refinery authorization (at gas stations, three-month implementation) is the primary Russian domestic mitigation in effect. The IEA dual shock — Hormuz Blockade Day 3 plus Omsk Day 17 — is compounding at its peak adverse point simultaneously. The bridge strikes on Iran add a potential new supply-chain shock channel: if Iran-Iraq border bridges were targeted, Iraqi oil export logistics and Russian equipment resupply routes through Iraq are affected. Fourth: Aspen Security Forum concludes today. The forum's final day sessions (July 17) address the full arc: six consecutive exchange nights, Tehran strikes, bridge targeting, Kharg Island disinformation, and Lebanon Pilot Zones. The forum's policy output — if any — may signal Washington expert consensus on the Kharg Island landing risk-benefit calculation. Fifth: Venezuela earthquake Day 24 — 1,719+ confirmed dead, 46,600+ missing; Operation Miracle access to remote areas ongoing. Sixth: Colombia T-21 to de la Espriella inauguration (August 7).

items.summary: The July 17 morning economic register is dominated by the Warsh three-condition framework's continued simultaneous adverse state and the potential new economic shock introduced by bridge targeting. On the rate outlook: CME FedWatch September rate hike odds stood at 68.8% as of July 16 evening, the highest sustained probability since the blockade reinstatement. Warsh's three stated conditions for a September hold (Hormuz normalization, Russian refining recovery, commodity price relief) are simultaneously worsening on Day 3 of the blockade. First condition — Hormuz normalization — is maximally adverse: blockade Day 3 active, six consecutive exchange nights, no diplomatic channel. Second condition — Russian refining recovery — is maximally adverse: Omsk Day 17, 75% offline, mini-refinery authorization is a three-month timeline. Third condition — commodity relief — is in adverse territory: Brent estimated $84-86, WTI $79-81, both above the $72 normalization floor and the $76 Vibe-4 threshold. On bridge targeting: the overnight July 16-17 bridge strikes introduce a potential new economic disruption channel beyond the Strait blockade. If the bridge targets included Iran-Iraq border crossings — a likely component of supply-chain interdiction strategy — the economic effects would compound across three vectors. First: Iraqi oil export logistics through border crossings (Iraq exports approximately 3.3 million bpd, and road transport serves domestic refinery supply chains). Second: Russian resupply routes to Iran through Iraq (circumventing sanctions via land transit). Third: Iranian IRGC proxy network resupply channels to Lebanon, Syria, and Yemen (logistics backbone for Hezbollah, Hamas, and Houthi arms flows). None of these are immediately quantifiable in oil price terms, but the disruption potential is structurally larger than the prior coastal-military strike architecture. On the oil price: Brent was $84.63 on July 16 with a muted -0.37% response to the Tehran strikes. The bridge strikes are unlikely to produce a larger immediate reaction than the Tehran strikes did, given the market's established framework of 'horizontal escalation but not Strait-closing.' The primary oil price event risk remains the Kharg Island Marine landing decision (WTI to $100+ if executed, per July 16 analysis). The IRGC's 'oil for everyone or no one' threat — Bab el-Mandeb activation via Houthis — is the secondary event risk: if executed, it would add Red Sea closure to the Hormuz blockade, producing a dual-strait closure not seen since the 2024 Houthi campaign at its peak. Neither risk has materialized. Jackson Hole (August 22-24, T-36 from today) is the next major Warsh communications event. July CPI (releasing approximately August 14, T-28, 8 days before Jackson Hole) will be the only additional inflation data point Warsh receives before speaking. July CPI will measure energy prices during the blockade-era WTI range of $79-81 — structurally adverse to any dovish Jackson Hole signal.

items.summary: Four secondary economic-legislative threads on July 17 morning. First: USTR Section 301 completion deadline T-3 (July 20). Three days to deadline with no finalization announced. The White House's policy bandwidth on July 17 is consumed by the sixth consecutive night of Iran strikes, bridge targeting assessment, Iran disinformation management, and the Kharg Island Marine landing decision timeline — all generating simultaneous NSC and IC demand. USTR's July 20 deadline is statute-equivalent and does not extend on geopolitical grounds; the Iran crisis does not create legal authority to delay the tariff-framework transition. Without White House sign-off on the final Section 301 structure (proposed: 12.5% on 46 countries, 10% on 15 including EU, Canada, UK, Mexico), the July 20 deadline creates a 3-4 day importer planning uncertainty gap before the Section 122 July 24 expiry — the highest-risk tariff compliance window of the 2026 arc. Second: FERC AI 30-day nominal deadline T-1 (July 18 — tomorrow). The six ISO/RTOs are in their final preparation day for the July 18 nominal deadline (Saturday; generation adequacy reports officially due Monday July 20 — first business day). PNW Climate Week Day 5 is today — the forum's penultimate day (Days 5-6, July 17-18) runs through the FERC nominal deadline and creates a policy forum-and-regulatory-deadline convergence window. The PJM July 3 data center curtailment emergency (160 million people affected) anchors all six submissions. Any early ISO/RTO submission today or tomorrow provides the first formal national accounting of AI large-load integration readiness before the July 20 actual deadline. FERC's 60-day show-cause enforcement deadline (August 17) makes the July 20 submissions the gateway to potential enforcement action. Third: OBBB Law Day 18. Medicaid work requirements and SNAP restrictions active in 18 states; zero federal stays. Aragon v. Rollins (SNAP food restriction, five states) is T-14 from the July 31 SNAP effective date — the statutory collision between OBBB mandate and federal court USDA authority ruling is approaching its enforcement deadline without judicial resolution.
